name: Erastin
mechanism_of_action: System Xc- inhibition depletes intracellular cystine, collapsing glutathione synthesis and inducing ferroptosis

interactions.curator_notes: Cystine withdrawal combined with the system Xc- inhibitor erastin in the source study's cell-line panel; combined ferroptotic death was ferrostatin-1-rescuable (Swanda et al. 2023). Quantitative per-line viability/dose data pending curation from source figures; note erastin also blocks cystine uptake, so the two legs act on an overlapping node (system Xc-) rather than fully independent pathways.

[Mechanistic Bridging -- model-generated hypothesis, not a tested result] Glucose restriction (5% of standard medium glucose) induces a nrf2_ferroptosis signature (death_promoting) in T47D; Erastin's reported resistance mechanism runs through the same pathway (GPX4-dependent lipid-peroxide detoxification). Because the modifier's effect on this pathway is death-promoting (suppresses the pathway the drug's resistance depends on), this is surfaced as a synergy candidate. This combination has not been evaluated together in any cited study -- it is a candidate for testing, generated by matching independently-curated signature and resistance-mechanism evidence, not a direct or inferred empirical finding.
interactions.modifier_agent: Glucose restriction (5% of standard medium glucose)

resistance_mechanism.mechanism_description: GPX4 detoxifies lipid peroxides downstream of cystine/glutathione depletion; sufficient GPX4 activity (or an intact glutathione pool feeding it) can rescue cells from erastin's system Xc- blockade despite cystine starvation (Dixon et al. 2012; Yang et al. 2014).

interactions.curator_notes: [Mechanistic Bridging -- model-generated hypothesis, not a tested result] Serine/glycine starvation (-SG medium; dietary serine/glycine depletion in vivo) induces a nrf2_ferroptosis signature (protective_resistance) in HCT116; Erastin's reported resistance mechanism runs through the same pathway (GPX4-dependent lipid-peroxide detoxification). Because the modifier's effect on this pathway is protective/resistance-conferring (reinforces the same pathway the drug's resistance depends on), this predicts antagonism and is logged here rather than surfaced as a synergy candidate. This combination has not been evaluated together in any cited study -- it is a candidate for testing, generated by matching independently-curated signature and resistance-mechanism evidence, not a direct or inferred empirical finding.
